title: Microsoft Purview DLP: aggregate alerts by user (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, alert settings, licensing and documented behaviour are supported, and it explicitly reports the differences between the roadmap and Learn. Two checklist items refer to controls missing from the controls table; these are minor completeness findings.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes consolidating related DLP alert events for a common user into one alert object.
claims.quote: Enable aggregation of DLP alerts based on common entities user even when multiple rules are matched. This feature should consolidate related alert events into a single alert object

claims.quote: enhance contextual understanding of violations.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enabling user-based aggregation in tenant-level DLP settings aggregates single-event alerts by user.
claims.quote: When you enable user based alert aggration in DLP setting at the tenant level, single event alerts are aggregated based on users.

claims.claim: Rule matches must occur within an admin-configurable tenant-level window of 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes.
claims.quote: The rule match events must occur within the configurable time window (15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes). This time window is configurable by the admin at the tenant level.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn describes alert generation per rule match event per user, unlike the roadmap's cross-rule description.
claims.quote: Alerts are generated per rule match event per user.

claims.claim: Without user-based aggregation, the documented E5 single-rule aggregation window is one minute.
claims.quote: By default when events from a single rule occur in a one minute window of each other they are aggregated for E5 license and 15 mins for E3 license.

claims.claim: Without user-based aggregation, the documented E3 single-rule aggregation window is 15 minutes.
claims.quote: These windows are not configurable by the admin-E5: 60 seconds-E3: 15 minutes

claims.claim: User-based aggregation does not apply to threshold-based aggregate-event alerts.
claims.quote: Threshold based aggregation - Aggregate DLP rule matches based on count of matches. - User based alert aggregation not applicable.

claims.claim: Learn says to expect increased alert volume for the single-user-per-rule option.
claims.quote: For single user per rule. - Expect an increase in alert volume.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A new match for the same user and rule within the aggregation window is added to the same alert even if it was closed.
claims.quote: If the alert is closed within the aggregation time window and a new match occurs for the same user and rule, then the new rule match will be aggregated into the same alert.

claims.claim: The supplied description presents aggregation as grouping alert events, not as an action on users or content.
claims.quote: This feature should consolidate related alert events into a single alert object to: Reduce alert noise, simplify investigation workflows, enhance contextual understanding of violations.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends the Defender XDR dashboard for investigating DLP alerts.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard is the recommended location for investigating and managing DLP alerts.

claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches the rule's Send an alert to admins when a rule match occurs control.
claims.quote: Scroll down to the Incident reports section and toggle Send an alert to admins when a rule match occurs to On. Email alerts are automatically sent to the administrator and anyone else you add to the list of recipients.

claims.quote: The GenerateAlert parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that notifies the specified users when the conditions of the rule are met. Valid values are: An email address. SiteAdmin. Type: MultiValuedProperty. The Identity parameter specifies the DLP rule that you want to modify.
